title: Three things the image model couldn’t do in my noir comic game, and how each got fixed
author: MDawg74
selftext:
https://reddit.com/link/1xafnzj/video/n7l3sf1q3jwh1/player

Unit 112 is a storage-auction and pawn-shop game told in comic panels. Free in the browser: [https://mdawg74.itch.io/unit-112](https://mdawg74.itch.io/unit-112)

All the art came from flux-1-schnell running on a free Cloudflare Workers AI account, called through a small worker. Roughly 650 images a day on the free tier. Every image gets looked at by a human before it ships, and that's where the problems showed up.

Keys. One panel had a ring of keys on a hallway floor. The model drew them the size of a dog with gibberish on the tag. Regenerating kept giving the same thing, so the keys got painted out and the floor rebuilt from the surrounding concrete.

Handwriting. The story runs on letters: a dead father's note, a landlord's apology, a ledger with "Behind 2 mo. Don't tell the kid." The model writes scribbles that look like text from across the room. Fix: erase the page, draw the ruled lines and the words flat in a handwriting font, then warp the sheet onto the page's perspective so it sits on the lines. One base image became seven different letters, each saying what its caption says.

People walking away. Customers leave the shop on screen, so I asked for figures seen from behind. About a third came back facing the camera anyway. Those were rerolled until the backs were backs.

The code was written with AI too. A bot plays 120 runs per play style to tune the economy, which is how I found the price estimates were making everyone overpay.

The design and direction are mine. Solo project, my entry in the Game Gauntlet SIM Jam.
